{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Commerce One / Corio Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Corio)  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.5 — verified findings and recommended positions

## Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement acting for Corio as the customer/licensee. Overall the commercial architecture is workable, and several areas of common concern are clean: there is no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us, no non-compete or field-of-use restraint, no most-favoured-nation obligation and no liquidated damages or penalty payable by us.

Two issues are critical. First, Section 13.5 vests Developments in Corio but then carves out Developments "supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One" — the effect is an assignment of IP we create and fund to the Vendor, which our playbook treats as a walk-away item. Second, the Section 9 liability cap is nominally mutual but illusory: it is limited to amounts "actually paid" by Corio and only for "the transaction which the liability relates to", with no floor, and the only carve-out is Commerce One's IP indemnity — confidentiality, data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud all sit inside the cap.

High-priority items are the symmetric assignment bar in Section 14.1 (no affiliate carve-out for us, and a competitor carve-back that lets Commerce One block our M&A assignment), the absence of any Affiliate/contractor extension of the Section 2 licences, and the lack of any convenience exit from a five-year term terminable only for breach or insolvency. Medium items cover arbitration (we accept California law but want courts), the scope of the Vendor indemnity, the 60-day/31 December 1999 warranty sunset, renewal pricing, MarketSite.net annual access fees across the full five-year term, and the absence of any transition assistance or data-return obligation. Low items are audit mechanics and vendor insurance.

One finding (non-solicitation) failed verification and is retained as internal evidence only pending confirmation of the ancillary documents.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue and position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 13 Shared Resources | Carve-out transfers ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One where it supports them on an ongoing basis. Delete the carve-out and repair the sentence; Commerce One's pre-existing materials and Software ownership (§ 2.8) are unaffected. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 9 Limitation of Liability | Cap tied to amounts "actually paid" by Corio for "the transaction which the liability relates to", with no floor and carve-outs limited to § 8. Set cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and add standard uncapped Excluded Claims; mutual exclusion of indirect damages left intact. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14 Miscellaneous | § 14.1 gives us no affiliate carve-out or reasonableness standard, and the competitor carve-back lets Commerce One block our merger or asset-sale assignment. Give Corio affiliate/successor assignment without consent; confine consent and the competitor bar to Commerce One. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 3 (2. Grant of Rights) | Grants run to Corio only; no Affiliate definition and § 2.2 is confined to Corio's internal business operations. Insert new § 2.11 extending the Section 2 licences to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, with Corio responsible for their compliance. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 11 Term and Termination | Five-year initial term with automatic one-year renewals; termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency, with no refund of prepaid fees. Add § 11.4 giving Corio a 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund and no early-termination penalty. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 3 (2. Grant of Rights) | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Corio; grants are non-exclusive and Exhibit D cooperation is expressly non-binding. No redline. Revisit if the redacted figures in § 2.4 contain an exclusivity condition. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 4 Fees | No liquidated damages, penalty, late-payment interest or termination fee payable by us; § 4.4 audit cost-shifting is not liquidated damages. No redline. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 3 (2. Grant of Rights) | Only ordinary licence-scope limits and Territory/Market Segment definitions; § 13.6 preserves independent development and § 14.8 confirms subcontracting rights. No redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 14 Miscellaneous | California law is acceptable (fallback), but mandatory single-arbitrator AAA arbitration is not. Retain California law and San Francisco, substitute exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts, and conform the § 12 escrow cross-reference to § 14.3. |
| Medium | INDEMN — Vendor indemnification | Deviation | § 8 Indemnification | IP infringement indemnity meets the fallback and is carved out of the § 9 cap, but limbs for breach of applicable law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access/disclosure of data and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and coverage of our affiliates, are absent. Insert § 8.3 adding those limbs under the § 8.1 procedure. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 8 (7. Warranties and Disclaimer) | Warranty runs 60 days from the Effective Date and is capped at 31 December 1999, so it may expire before or shortly after acceptance testing; no services warranty. Extend to 12 months from acceptance (removing the sunset) and add a services warranty with re-performance/repair/refund remedy. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 11 Term and Termination | Renewal length and the 30-day opt-out are acceptable, but there is no renewal reminder and no cap on renewal pricing (Exhibit B prices "Year 2-5, and beyond" with no uplift limit). Add a 60-day reminder and cap uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%, with 5% as fallback. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | Missing | § 11 Term and Termination | No transition assistance or data-return obligation; § 11.3 is only a mutual confidential-information return/destroy right and gives Commerce One a destruction option. Insert § 11.4: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable data return within 30 days, then deletion with written certification (90-day fallback). |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Deviation | § 17 Payment Terms | No take-or-pay or user cap, but the fixed annual MarketSite.net access fee runs across a five-year term we can exit only for breach or insolvency. Take the fallback: 30 days' notice right to reduce or discontinue access with pro-rata true-up rather than a penalty. |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 4 Fees | No most-favoured-nation or price-parity obligation on us; Exhibit D cooperation is non-binding. No redline. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 13 Shared Resources | No non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant found; § 13 and § 14 were read in full and Exhibit D § 5 imposes no hiring restriction. Retained as internal evidence only: the integration clause incorporates the Non Disclosure Agreement and Statement of Work, which are not in this file and should be confirmed on the deal record. |
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 4 Fees | § 4.4 already meets our position on frequency, auditor independence and cost allocation, but notice is only "reasonable", timing only "reasonable times", and the auditor is not bound by confidentiality. Add 30 days' written notice, business-hours limitation, auditor confidentiality and off-site/no-systems-access wording. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 14 Miscellaneous | No insurance provision, despite on-site consultants, implementation services and Commerce One's operation of MarketSite.net. Insert a short covenant after § 14.9 (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), renumbering existing 14.10. Fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

## Walk-away items

- **Assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor (§ 13.5).** The "unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One" carve-out turns a support arrangement into a title transfer of IP we create and fund. Our playbook treats assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor as a walk-away; the carve-out must be struck. We can live with the residual sentence leaving ownership of enhancements to the Software itself to be negotiated, as those are derivative works of Commerce One's licensed Software.

No other finding is flagged as a walk-away. In particular, the arbitration clause is a medium deviation only, since the seat is domestic.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** on the two critical items first — deletion of the § 13.5 carve-out and the § 9 cap reset (greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, plus standard uncapped Excluded Claims, confirming Corio's fee obligations are not damages subject to the cap).
2. **Table the high-priority package** together: § 14.1 assignment rewrite, new § 2.11 Affiliate/contractor licence extension, and new § 11.4 convenience termination with pro-rata refund.
3. **Obtain an unredacted copy** of § 2.4 and Exhibit B. Our exclusivity conclusion is based on redacted figures ([*]) and should be revisited if the redacted text in § 2.4 contains any exclusivity condition.
4. **Confirm the ancillary documents.** The integration clause incorporates the Non Disclosure Agreement and the Statement of Work, neither of which is in this file; we need to confirm on the deal record that neither carries a personnel covenant before we close out the non-solicitation finding.
5. **Sequence the medium items** as a single mark-up: courts in place of AAA arbitration (retaining California law and San Francisco, and conforming the § 12 cross-reference), new § 8.3 indemnity limbs, 12-month warranty from acceptance plus services warranty, renewal reminder and uplift cap, MarketSite.net reduction right, and the § 11.4 transition and data-return provisions.
6. **Hold the low items** (audit mechanics, vendor insurance) as trade material, with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M insurance fallback available if resisted.
7. **Prepare fallbacks** in advance for the likely pressure points: 5% renewal uplift cap, 90 days' transition assistance, and — if Commerce One proposes a personnel covenant — a mutual, 12-month restriction limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire."}
